beats.intro: Learning module two. [[sub]]The main derivative instruments, and the payoffs they create.
beats.firm: [[head]]Forwards, futures and swaps are firm commitments: both sides are obliged to perform. [[f1]]Each has a specific contract size, [[f2]]a specific underlying, [[f3]]one or more exchanges on future dates, [[f4]]and a price agreed today. [[k1]]A forward is a single, customized O T C exchange. [[k2]]A future is a standardized forward, traded on an exchange. [[k3]]And a swap is a series of exchanges.
beats.fwdpay: [[axes]]Here is the payoff of a forward at maturity. Across, the spot price at maturity, S sub T. Up, the payoff. [[f0]]The forward price, F sub zero of T, is agreed at the start. [[long]]The buyer, who is long, receives S sub T minus the forward price. Above the forward price, a gain. Below it, a loss. [[short]]The seller's payoff is the exact mirror image. [[nocash]]Nothing is paid upfront, so payoff equals profit. [[linear]]And because the payoff is a straight line in the underlying, firm commitments are called linear derivatives.
beats.gold: [[head]]An example. Procam Investments agrees to buy one hundred ounces of gold in three months, at a forward price of one thousand seven hundred ninety-two dollars and thirteen cents an ounce. [[spot]]Today's spot price, seventeen seventy, plays no role in the settlement. [[st]]At maturity, gold is at seventeen eighty dollars fifty. [[pay]]The payoff per ounce is S sub T minus the forward price: minus eleven dollars sixty-three. [[total]]Times one hundred ounces, Procam pays the dealer one thousand one hundred sixty-three dollars.
beats.futures: [[ex]]Now the same trade as a futures contract on an exchange. [[im]]No price is paid upfront, but each side deposits initial margin: four thousand nine hundred fifty dollars. [[mtm]]Every day the clearinghouse marks the contract to market. On day one, the futures price rises five dollars. [[gain]]Procam, the buyer, gains five hundred dollars, credited to its margin account. [[loss]]The seller loses five hundred. Its balance falls to four thousand four hundred fifty, [[mm]]below the maintenance margin of four thousand five hundred. [[call]]That triggers a margin call: the seller must top up five hundred dollars, back to the initial margin. This top up is called variation margin.
beats.margin: [[head]]Follow Procam's margin account to maturity. [[d1]]Day one, a gain: five thousand four hundred fifty. [[d2]]Day two, the price drops ten dollars eighty-eight. The balance falls below maintenance, [[c1]]so Procam pays a margin call of five hundred eighty-eight. [[d3]]Two more down days, [[c2]]and a second call, eight hundred eighty. [[d5]]Then two small gains. [[sum]]In total, Procam paid one thousand four hundred sixty-eight in margin calls, and gets back three hundred five more than it deposited. The net loss is one thousand one hundred sixty-three, exactly the forward's loss. [[timing]]Only the timing of the cash flows differs.
beats.rules: [[head]]A few more futures rules. [[r1]]Exchanges can raise margins, or call for margin during the day. [[r2]]Price limits stop trading outside a band around the previous settlement price. A circuit breaker pauses trading for a while. [[r3]]To exit early, a trader simply enters the offsetting contract. [[r4]]And at expiration, physical delivery or cash settlement makes the futures price converge to the spot price.
beats.swaps: [[pair]]A swap is a series of exchanges. The fixed rate payer pays a fixed rate, the swap rate. The floating rate payer pays a market reference rate. [[periods]]Each period, the fixed payment stays the same, [[float]]while the floating payment resets with the market. [[series]]So a swap is like a series of forward contracts, one for each payment date.
beats.fyleton: [[head]]Fyleton Investments enters a five-year swap on two hundred million pounds. It receives a fixed two point two five percent, paid semiannually, and pays six-month M R R. [[fix]]The fixed leg for one half-year: two hundred million times two point two five percent, divided by two. Two point two five million pounds. [[flt]]M R R is set at one point nine five percent, so the floating leg is one point nine five million. [[net]]The payments are netted: the dealer pays Fyleton three hundred thousand pounds. [[notional]]The notional itself is never exchanged. It only sizes the payments. [[zero]]At inception the swap is worth zero to both sides. As rates move, one side gains value and the other loses.
beats.options: [[right]]Options are contingent claims. The buyer has the right, but not the obligation, to transact. The seller must perform if the buyer chooses. [[prem]]For that right, the buyer pays a premium upfront. Say five dollars, for a call: the right to buy a stock at an exercise price of thirty. [[up]]If the stock ends at forty, the buyer exercises: a payoff of ten, a profit of five. [[down]]If it ends at twenty-five, the buyer walks away and loses only the five dollar premium. [[styles]]A European option can be exercised only at maturity. An American option can be exercised at any time. [[cp]]A call is the right to buy; a put is the right to sell.
beats.longcall: [[axes]]The long call at maturity. [[payoff]]The payoff is the maximum of zero and S sub T minus X. Flat at zero below the exercise price, then rising one for one. [[profit]]Subtract the premium to get profit. The most the buyer can lose is the premium. [[be]]Profit is zero at the breakeven point, X plus the premium. [[hi]]Hightest's index call has an exercise price of twelve forty, and cost twenty-four eighty-five. [[pts]]At twelve eighty, the payoff is forty and the profit fifteen fifteen. At twelve sixty, a payoff of twenty, but a loss of four eighty-five. At or below twelve forty, the whole premium is lost. [[nonlin]]This bent, asymmetric shape is why options are called non-linear derivatives.
beats.money: [[line]]Before maturity, compare the spot price with the exercise price. [[itm]]A call is in the money when the spot price is above X. Its exercise value, or intrinsic value, is S minus X. [[atm]]At the money means S equals X, [[otm]]and out of the money means S is below X. Both have zero intrinsic value. [[tv]]Yet the option still has a price. That extra is time value: the chance that the price moves favorably before maturity. Time value shrinks to zero at expiration.
beats.shortcall: [[mirror]]The call seller's profit is the mirror image. [[max]]The most the seller can earn is the premium, [[unl]]and the loss is unlimited as the underlying rises. [[credit]]Credit risk runs one way. Once the premium is paid, the seller has no exposure to the buyer. But the buyer depends on the seller to pay at maturity.
beats.puts: [[axes]]A put is the right to sell at X. [[payoff]]Its payoff is the maximum of zero and X minus S sub T: it pays when the price falls. [[profit]]Subtract the premium for profit, with breakeven at X minus the premium. [[short]]The put seller's profit mirrors it. The maximum gain is the premium. [[maxloss]]The loss is large, but limited, because a price cannot fall below zero. With an exercise price of thirty and a premium of five, the seller can lose at most twenty-five.
beats.cds: [[pair]]Credit derivatives transfer the risk that a borrower defaults. In a credit default swap, the protection buyer pays a fixed spread, [[spread]]say one hundred basis points a year, to the protection seller. [[event]]If a credit event occurs, such as bankruptcy or failure to pay, the seller pays the loss given default times the notional. [[ins]]It works much like insurance. The buyer is short credit risk; the seller is long credit risk, like a bondholder. [[mig]]If the issuer's credit spread widens to two hundred fifty basis points, the buyer is still paying only one hundred. The contract has gained value for the buyer, and lost value for the seller.
beats.compare: [[axes]]Forward commitments and contingent claims can create similar exposures. [[fwd]]Here is a long forward, [[call]]and a long call with an exercise price equal to the forward price. [[up]]When the price rises, the forward earns more, because the call buyer paid a premium. [[down]]When it falls far enough, the call is better: its loss stops at the premium. [[cross]]They cross where S sub T minus the forward price equals minus the premium. [[put]]A short put also gains when prices rise, but its upside is capped at the premium received.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]Forwards, futures and swaps are firm commitments with linear payoffs. [[w2]]Futures are marked to market daily through margin accounts. [[w3]]Options give the buyer a right for a premium: the payoffs are non-linear. [[w4]]Credit default swaps transfer default risk, much like insurance.
beats.finish: That's the end of learning module two.
